key_insight: Electric–magnetic dipole interference can generate spin and charge photocurrents in centrosymmetric crystals without breaking inversion symmetry.
engineering_relevance: This mechanism could expand photovoltaic and optoelectronic functionality in inversion-symmetric materials such as cubic silicon and cubic SrTiO3.
method: Develop a unified microscopic theory of electric–magnetic dipole interference.
Combine symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations.
Separate shift-like and injection-like currents and classify symmetry and polarization dependence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports calculated responses that scale linearly with light intensity and are roughly 10⁻³–10⁻² as strong as conventional non-centrosymmetric responses, yet predicted to be experimentally accessible.
watch_item: The weak signal requires experimental validation; the abstract reports neither solar-cell efficiency gains nor an AI method.
paper_title: Spin and Charge Photocurrents from Electric-Magnetic Dipole Interference in Centrosymmetric Crystals
